uncited: The system maintains a logical grouping of nodes.
- **Slice Assignment:** Each group is assigned a specific subset of slices from the volume.
Each group $g_i$ contains one host node $H_i$ and several slave nodes $S_{i,1} \dots S_{i,k}$.
**Slice Allocation:** Assign a disjoint subset of slices to each group.
There is no synchronization between groups during processing.
**Progress Broadcasting:** When a group finishes processing a slice, its host broadcasts a message to all other group hosts.
**Capacity Broadcasting:** When a group has only half a slice of work remaining, its host broadcasts a message to other group hosts indicating that the group is nearly full.
- The nodes of the finished group are re-assigned as slave nodes to other unfinished groups.
- **Time Complexity:** The scheme reduces idle time by dynamically balancing load.
- **Memory Complexity:** Memory usage is proportional to the number of nodes and the size of the slice subsets assigned to each group.
It was developed to address the limitations of static partitioning strategies (symmetry and host-slave) in distributed memory environments.
